sources.quote: it reports connecting more than two million people a year with community and social services
sources.title: About 211 – 211 Canada
sources.evidence: Every year, 211 connects over 2 million Canadians to the help they need most. 211 is a free, confidential service that provides everyone in Canada with easy access to information about essential government and community services; you can dial 2-1-1 to connect to community services near you.

sources.quote: Google Ad Grants offers eligible nonprofits up to USD $10,000 per month of in-kind Search advertising
sources.title: Ad Grants: $10,000 USD in Google Ads Credits - Google for Nonprofits
sources.evidence: Google Ad Grants provides up to $10,000 USD per month of in-kind search advertising for qualifying nonprofits. To qualify, your organization must be an eligible nonprofit, have a high-quality website that meets Google's website policy, and be able to meet the program policies.

sources.quote: Government entities, hospitals and schools are generally ineligible, though an affiliated foundation may qualify
sources.title: Eligibility guidelines - Google for Nonprofits Help
sources.evidence: Governmental entities or organizations, hospitals or healthcare organizations, and schools, academic institutions, or universities are not eligible for Google for Nonprofits. Charitable arms or foundations associated with healthcare organizations are eligible, and philanthropic arms of educational organizations are also eligible.

sources.quote: a click-through rate floor, no single-word keywords, required geo-targeting and conversion tracking
sources.title: Account management policy - Google for Nonprofits Help
sources.evidence: Ad Grants accounts must maintain a 5% click-through rate (CTR) each month at the account level; if the CTR requirement isn't met for 2 consecutive months, your account will be temporarily deactivated. Single keywords aren't permitted under the mission-based policy except for brand terms and other exceptions; proper location settings include specific geo-targeting; and your account must have conversion tracking set up, reporting at least 1 conversion per month.

sources.quote: CG-013 assesses fundraising cost as a share of fundraising revenue: generally acceptable below roughly a third, open to scrutiny above that, rarely acceptable at the high end
sources.title: Fundraising by registered charities - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: A ratio of costs to revenue of 35% and above will prompt the CRA to examine the average ratio over recent years to determine if there is a trend of high fundraising costs. A ratio of costs to revenue above 70% will raise concerns with the CRA, and the charity must be able to provide an explanation and rationale for this level of expenditure to show that it is not engaged in unacceptable fundraising.

sources.quote: CG-027 permits unlimited public policy dialogue and development activities
sources.title: Public policy dialogue and development activities by charities - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: Charities may now pursue their stated charitable purposes by carrying on unlimited public policy dialogue and development activities in furtherance of those purposes. There is no limit on the amount of resources your charity can devote to PPDDAs, as long as the PPDDAs further your stated charitable purposes and your charity does not directly or indirectly support or oppose any political party or candidate for public office. The 2018 amendments (Bill C-86, Royal Assent December 13, 2018) replaced the provision that effectively limited charities to devoting only 10 per cent of their resources to non-partisan political activities.

sources.quote: Messages whose primary purpose is raising funds for a registered charity sit outside CASL's consent and unsubscribe requirements
sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions about Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation | CRTC
sources.evidence: There is an exemption under section 3(g) of the Governor-in-Council Regulations for CEMs sent by or on behalf of a registered charity, as defined under the Income Tax Act, where the primary purpose of the CEM is to raise funds for the charity. Such CEMs are excluded from section 6 of CASL. The principal purpose of the CEM must be to raise funds for the charity.

sources.title: Fundraising and solicitation responsibilities | Alberta.ca
sources.evidence: The Charitable Fund-raising Act sets standards for charitable organizations and professional fund-raisers when they solicit contributions. You must register as a charitable organization in Alberta if you intend to raise more than $25,000 in gross contributions in your financial year from solicitations to individuals in Alberta, or you will use the services of a fund-raising business. All fundraising businesses must be licensed in Alberta and provide a $25,000 security; if a fundraising business is used, donors must be told its operating and legal name and how its pay is determined.
